artifacts.synopsis: TE Williams appealed Chesapeake Presbytery's approval of his deposition from office and suspension from the Sacraments after trial on three charges (failure to manage household, slander, inappropriate behavior). The SJC denied all five specifications of error and upheld the Presbytery's decision in whole.

artifacts.synopsis: TE John Hardie appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Metro Atlanta Presbytery's judicial commission, raising seventeen specifications of error under six categories including procedural irregularities, improper evidence, refusal of indulgence, prejudice, and disproportionate censure. The SJC denied the appeal, finding no clear error in MAP's proceedings and upholding the indefinite suspension.

artifacts.title: Hedman v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: RE Gerald Hedman complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery unconstitutionally adopted five not-guilty verdicts regarding TE Peter Leithart's teachings on baptism, covenants, imputation, justification, and union with Christ. The SJC denied the complaint, finding it was bound by the Record of the Case and that Complainant had not demonstrated clear error on the part of Presbytery, with concurring and dissenting opinions discussing the scope of review, standing, and concerns about Leithart's sacramental theology.

artifacts.synopsis: Appeal by TE Paul W. Lee against Korean Southwest Presbytery's judgment finding him guilty of disobeying citations, rejecting admonitions, and other charges. The Standing Judicial Commission found KSWP erred on all issues through procedural violations including improper admonishment of judicial commission members mid-trial, failure to record trial proceedings, denial of cross-examination rights, and improper censure. Case remanded for retrial or dismissal.

artifacts.title: Adams v. Northeast Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Philip J. Adams complained about a Northeast Presbytery judicial matter while a related appeal was pending and sought a retrial of charges on which the accused had been acquitted. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order under BCO 43-1 and because the requested relief was unavailable. A separate opinion concurred in the result but dissented from part of the reasoning and urged clarification of appellate review after an acquittal.

artifacts.synopsis: Dr. Robert Shive appealed his conviction and excommunication after Christ Covenant Church found him guilty of sinful and sexually inappropriate speech toward two patients. The SJC found no reversible error in the trial, but held that the record did not show contumacy or impenitence sufficient for excommunication, reversed that censure, and remanded for indefinite suspension from the sacraments under BCO 36-5; a dissent was recorded.
